A security vulnerability is a weakness in software, configuration, or process that violates an intended security policy—often enabling confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact when exploited.

In shipped products, the same word shows up across different surfaces: vulnerable dependencies, vulnerable first-party code, and vulnerable runtime configurations—each has different discovery tooling (see Security/DevSecOps/Taxonomy).
Imported components — Software/Composition/Analysis and dependency vulnerability scanning match versions to advisories (GHSA, NVD, OSV ecosystems).
Your source — Security/Application/SAST flags bug classes in code under review.
Running behavior — Security/Application/DAST (and adjacent IAST / observability) finds issues that appear only when the system executes with real routing, auth state, and infrastructure.
“One scanner type covers the SDLC” — False; composition, static, and dynamic views are complementary, not interchangeable.
“No CVEs in the report means no vulns” — False; coverage gaps, unreachable but reported noise, and zero-day windows all apply.
